parsed.explanation: A small self-governing territory whose received legal regime accepts foreign documents under self-determination-based recognition, issues X markers, prohibits gender-identity discrimination (2024 law with a board), and criminalises gender-based hate speech with penalty enhancement. Marriage is accessible to trans visitors. No trans-specific criminal offence, no facility or border restriction, and documented low-key, integrated, non-violent social climate since 2010. Weaknesses are evidentiary, not expositional: no documented enforcement of the hate-crime or discrimination provisions, no record of X-marker issuance in practice, and silence on facilities, custody placement and healthcare access. Per rule 13, thin-data silence in a well-governed, protective-framework jurisdiction extrapolates toward the risk the structural facts imply — low — but the unverified complaint mechanism and undocumented custody/facility practice hold it below the 0.85–0.95 anchors with documented operating remedies. No visitor-facing exposure is documented; the residual is open questions, not exposure.
